title: Second-Order Excess Risk of Sequential Adaptive Experiments for Treatment Effect Estimation
banked_reason: D0.5 kernel_substituted: the advertised exact unrestricted minimax frontier was replaced by a one-sided log-free upper bound, while the unrestricted centered converse remained open.
gap_reasons: The advertised exact unrestricted minimax frontier is replaced by a one-sided log-free upper bound; retain the upper result only after retitling and positioning it as such, or supply the missing centered converse.
fixing variances freezes only Phi; zero-target mean bumps still vary Var_P(h_P(X))/n at the target second-order scale.

proof_attempt_summary: Discovery derived a law-independent, smoothness-adaptive sequential construction giving the claimed log-free two-nuisance upper rate, plus sharper mean-only upper regimes. The exact frontier collapsed because ordinary Assouad/constrained-risk and fixed-design arguments do not survive subtraction of the law-dependent oracle benchmark or the infimum over all non-anticipating designs. A future proposal must begin with an explicit uniform-over-design sequential Bayes information-regret converse rather than reuse the present lower-bound carrier.
tldr: One law-independent sequential algorithm, not using \(s\) or \(r\), attains for every fixed smoothness pair the constructive log-free upper rate \(n^{-1-2s/(2s+d)}\vee n^{-1-2r/(2r+d)}\) in the unrestricted oracle-subtracted excess-MSE decision problem. If one and the same known allocation, independent of the law and both smoothness indices, is pointwise oracle-optimal throughout the union of model classes, a smoothness-agnostic AIPW construction attains the sharper mean-only upper rate \(n^{-1-2s/(2s+d)}\). Equal conditional variance and pointwise singleton-support weights furnish such allocations. These are upper results: no positive centered converse over all measurable, possibly biased estimators, and hence no exact causal minimax order, is claimed.
gap: Li and Simchi-Levi's Section 4.4 Theorem 4.6, equations (16)--(18), remains logarithmically slack, and Theorem 4.7, equation (19), quantifies over an unbiased estimator pair and uses an excess-variance loss. Appendix F, Lemma F.6, equation (78), assumes local unbiasedness and substitutes exact centering in its proof. Their nuisance-rate assumption also does not derive the rate for learning a conditional variance in the presence of an unknown rough mean.
fill: The common minimax experiment fixes law-independent kernels before the superpopulation law and derives the observed filtration and propensities afterward. The reduction theorem matches its excess risk to two standalone nuisance minimax risks with no logarithm. The Brown--Low--Duchi--Ruan change-of-measure argument handles unrestricted estimators, while predictable cross-fitting and pairwise-difference local polynomials supply the attaining side. The absorption lemma yields the explicit frontier for every fixed dimension, and the univariate refinement imports the exact joint-smoothness variance rate.
